cells.label: Mera's lauta
cells.text: She set the lauta on the third stool, the one nobody claims, and unwound the ⟦oilcloth from its neck⟧ with fingers still white from the quay wind.

cells.label: The third verse
cells.text: The first verse settled the room. The second opened the windows of the past. The third ⟦called him down from the cold road⟧, and everyone knew to hold still.

cells.label: The wolf at the manor door
cells.text: He lowered his head beneath the lintel and did not enter. The audience watched the beast, and inside the beast, ⟦the man — his shame, his burden⟧, his recognition of the song.

cells.label: The geranium alleys
cells.text: Pots came in before dusk now. Children were not sent for water after the wind turned. The alleys kept their geraniums ⟦like held breath⟧.

cells.label: Brannic's cellar
cells.text: The cellar no one admits is a basement. Brannic counted barrels there in the dark, and ⟦one row he counted twice⟧ and never said why.

cells.label: The warm tin strip
cells.text: In the old dumbwaiter shaft a receiver tapped messages into strips of thin tin. When the cellar froze too hard for ink, Brannic read them ⟦by touch, like a blind man reading debts⟧.

cells.label: Below the barrels
cells.text: Seven days of silence. Then, at low tide, ⟦a tapping under the floor⟧ — patient, counted, like a man who knows morse and despair in equal measure.

cells.label: The oak plateau
cells.text: Two hours above the village, older than the roads that still remember the river's old course. The amphitheatre waited under the oaks ⟦as it had waited out the Thunderous Night⟧.

cells.label: The backstage corridor
cells.text: Corridors for musicians, mask-carriers, animal handlers, illusionists. Looted for centuries: garments, thunder drums, mirror rigs, ⟦delight engines built for wonder, not power⟧.

cells.label: The false moon pulley
cells.text: A mechanism to raise a moon that never was, so an audience could believe a night the sky refused. The rope has rotted, but ⟦the counterweight still hangs true⟧.

cells.label: The flute, remembered wrong
cells.text: The fragments disagree about the flute. One margin says it made audiences weep. Another says ⟦it could trap a person inside the shape others expect⟧. A third only says: made for theatre.

cells.label: X
cells.text: A starved, beaten-looking dog, ribs sharp under its skin, one ear torn, ⟦its eyes too human⟧ in the crude pencil work. At the bottom of the page, a single letter: X.
